title: Tenant priority weighting causes silent capacity starvation
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
BrightLens (Tier=Dedicated, reserved pool ID rp-eu-42) reported intermittent 5-12 minute cold starts and sustained 30-60% latency regressions during morning peak on 2026-02-17 -> 02-18. They opened an escalation after customer-visible errors increased and query latencies exceeded their SLOs.

What happened (short):
- Autoscaler failed to proactively allocate burst capacity for BrightLens despite observed tail-latency spikes.
- The safety-trigger logic (latency-based emergency scale) uses a smoothed metric (10-minute EMA) that filtered out sub-10m spikes. Those spikes coincided with short reserved-pool churn from other tenants.
- The allocation algorithm applies tenant-priority weighting and proportional-share rounding; a bug in the rounding step allowed low-weight tenants to claim fractional slots which were not reclaimed during headroom computation. Combined, the allocator thought there was sufficient headroom and did not trigger burst allocation for BrightLens.

Root cause (detailed):
1) Metrics smoothing: safety-trigger evaluates latency_ms_ema_10m and compares to safety_threshold_ms (150ms). BrightLens experienced 200-400ms tail spikes lasting 2-6 minutes. The 10m EMA reduced visibility and never crossed the threshold.
2) Priority-share rounding bug: when computing integer slot assignments from weighted shares we floor fractional results but failed to carry the leftover budget to higher-priority tenants. This led to silent starvation when many small-weight tenants occupy fractional allocations across the pool.
3) Burst budgeting interaction: burst_credit accounting was temporarily paused for tenants moving between host nodes during pool rebalancing; this window allowed low-priority tenants to consume more warm slots than intended.

Impact timeline and mitigation performed:
- 2026-02-17 09:12 UTC: BrightLens reported first elevated latencies.
- 2026-02-17 09:25 UTC: On-call triage (Sofia Martinez) gathered traces and repro steps.
- 2026-02-17 09:38 UTC: Emergency page to Allocator team. Noted EMA smoothing; immediately lowered safety_threshold to 120ms for affected pools as temporary mitigation.
- 2026-02-17 10:05 UTC: Manual burst-credit top-up applied for BrightLens (rp-eu-42) to provide immediate headroom. Latency improved within 6 minutes.
- 2026-02-17 11:40 UTC: Began incident debugging; discovered rounding behavior in share allocation algorithm.
- 2026-02-18 02:20 UTC: Deployed hotfix (infra PR #4123) to fix rounding carry logic and re-enable accurate fractional rebalancing in allocator.
- 2026-02-18 06:10 UTC: Monitored rollout to eu-west-1; BrightLens confirmed stable SLOs.

Hotfix and code references:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/4123 (fix: carry fractional remainder when computing tenant slot allocations)
- Rollout patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/9f3b2d7 (safety_threshold shorter window toggle)
- Quick telemetry query used during triage: grafana/dashboard/dedicated/autoscaler?var-pool=rp-eu-42 (referenced in links below)

Post-incident analysis and decisions so far:
- Short-term changes (merged/deployed):
  * Fix rounding carry in allocator (PR above).
  * Expose safety-trigger window as per-pool override; reduced default EMA window from 10m -> 3m for high-variance pools.
  * Added an emergency preempt path that allows burst-credit top-ups when tail latency > threshold for any tenant for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Monitoring/alerting added:
  * New alert: DedicatedPool:HighTailLatencyBurstCandidate fires when p95>150ms for 3m AND warm_slots_headroom<10%
  * New alert: Tenant:FracShareLeak detected when sum(fractional_remainder) > 0.8*pool_capacity for 5m
- Customer comms: Support sent BrightLens interim RCA and mitigation summary; scheduled technical review call 2026-03-02.

Open follow-ups / next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Add deterministic allocator unit tests covering fractional remainders and carry logic across random tenant distributions (Liam O'Neil).
- Implement e2e chaos test that simulates node churn + tenant move + rapid traffic spikes to validate preempt path (SRE).
- Evaluate aggressive EMA alternatives (EWMA with tunable alpha) and run A/B on low-latency/high-variance pools (Research/Serving).
- Create runbook entry: "When p95 > safety_threshold but EMA not breached" with playbook actions (oncall runbook editor).
- Audit burst-credit pause windows and eliminate any path that pauses credit updates during rebalancing (Allocator team).

Acceptance criteria for closure:
1) Unit + integration tests for allocator rounding logic merged and stable in CI.
2) New alerts firing in prod and validated by SRE run.
3) BrightLens confirms no SLO regressions for 30 days in their reserved pool.
4) Postmortem doc published and shared with Customer Success.

Notes and trade-offs considered:
- Lowering the EMA window increases sensitivity and may cause more scale churn—trade-off accepted for high-variance pools with clear SLO impact. We will monitor scale operations cost and tune per-pool.
- Emergency preempt path is intentionally conservative (3m) to avoid oscillation during flash traffic; long-term solution is smarter predictive scaling rather than shorter windows only.
